subject: Atlas Health launch: request for bridging credit due to private-connect delay
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara@atlashealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas launch delayed — request for remediation and next steps

Irene,

Quick note from our side — our integration team hit a blocker yesterday when we tried to bring up the private VPC connector in our staging environment. The connector is required for our compliance sign-off; without it we can't go live. Our timeline is now slipping at least three weeks and the program team is asking whether Redwood can provide a commercial remediation (credit or temporary rate) to cover lost launch marketing and integration costs.

We appreciate the product team's face-to-face last week and know the connector was promised in the roadmap for "late Aug," but we need something tangible today to keep our exec committee comfortable.

Can you advise on options (credit, extended trial, or other remedies)? Procurement is now looped in (procurement@atlashealth.com).

Thanks,
Sara Lee
Head of Partnerships
Atlas Health

Attachments: integration_failure_log.txt (referenced)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sara Lee <sara@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas launch delayed — request for remediation and next steps

Team — forwarding Sara's note. Summary: Atlas Health's go-live is blocked because our private/VPC connector isn't available in their region/test cluster; they now estimate a 2–3 week slip and are asking for a commercial remedy to keep the launch on track. I've attached their timeline and our latest SOW adjustments for context.

As this is a high-priority enterprise pilot (ATLAS-2027-08) and the ask is explicit, I'm proposing we discuss a short-term bridging credit while product delivers the connector. Proposed starter options (need cross-functional input):

- Option A: 30% credit off monthly usage for the first month post-launch (one-time invoice credit)
- Option B: 20% credit for two months + an engineering SLA commitment to prioritize the private connector in the Sept sprint
- Option C: No $ credit, extended trial/waived setup fee + additional RGAs in console (lower commercial impact)

Requesting: product to confirm ETA and risk (Karthik), finance to quantify P&L impact for the above (David), sales to recommend customer-facing language (Laura/Marissa), and Rishi for executive signoff threshold (how much can we approve without board/exec?). I'll hold off responding to Atlas until we sync.

Attachments: SOW_v2.pdf, atlas_integration_timeline.xlsx, proposal_draft.docx

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0182

Thanks for the heads up, Irene. Quick product update: the private VPC connector has progressed but we hit a compatibility regression with our network stack when enabling the new handoff for longseq sessions. Current realistic ETA for a safe rollout to Atlas' region is 2027-09-14 (we can try an earlier experimental patch, but it's not suitable for production).

Commercially, I recognize the constraint and recommend conditional remediation tied to a clear timeline:

- Proposal 1 (preferred): 25% usage credit for the first two billing cycles after customer launch, contingent on a signed amendment that (a) commits Atlas to a 12-month term extension and (b) accepts the specified delivery date in writing.
- Proposal 2: 15% credit for first month + waived setup fee if they cannot commit to extension.
- Engineering fallback: offer a temporary engineering hotfix under a paid SLA if Atlas is willing to accept a pre-GA patch (not recommended for regulated workloads).

If finance confirms the impacts, these options give us levers to protect revenue while preserving partnership goodwill. Laura/Marissa — you should present the conditional options to the customer; legal will need to draft a short amendment. Rishi — will you please advise what cap we have for commercial credits that don't require broader exec approval?

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the quick turn. Recommendation from commercial: move with Proposal 1 but tighten the terms slightly to limit downside. Specific ask for approval here:

- Approve a bridging credit of 25% off usage for two billing cycles after launch, conditioned on Atlas signing a 12-month extension amendment and explicit acceptance of delivery ETA (2027-09-14).
- Legal to draft a 2–3 sentence amendment and procurement to confirm signatures.
- Finance (David) — please confirm the expected revenue hit for this deal and whether we can approve up to $40k in total credits without needing finance committee escalation.

If Rishi can confirm we can sign off up to that threshold, we'll communicate to Atlas today and get the amendment signed — timing is tight to avoid the exec committee pushback on their side. Marissa, pls coordinate the message and flag any wording you want me to tweak.

Irene — once we have David/Rishi confirmation I'll send the customer note and the amendment link.

Thanks,
